author: @fl0rianr

evidence.api_compatibility: This is a breaking change for misconfigured installations. If a user has LEMONADE_API_KEY set to a non-empty value and LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY explicitly set to an empty string, requests that previously succeeded without authentication will now return 401. The PR author correctly flagged this in the Breaking Changes section: 'Only misconfigured installations with a non-empty LEMONADE_API_KEY and an explicitly empty LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY are affected.' No other configurations are changed. This is a correct tightening of security, not an API regression.
evidence.documentation: The PR states documentation is not affected, which is correct: this is a bug fix that tightens existing authentication behavior. No public-facing API contract or configuration guide change is needed. The breaking change is well-documented in the PR description with precise scope.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No evidence of manual end-to-end testing on a built server image. All CI checks passed (CodeQL, C++ unit tests, API key tests on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest, container smoke tests, build and packaging). The regression test is a unit-level test that starts the server in-process; it does not exercise a release candidate binary the way a tester would. Manual release testing is recommended (see to-dos).
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after the first (and only) approval. The PR contained a single commit (b2dd529) that matches the merge commit. No churn or scope creep.
evidence.review: One review from @superm1, submitted 2026-11-10T15:19:10Z, with APPROVED decision. @superm1 is a repository admin maintainer with subject area expertise in security and Docker/containers, matching the security nature of this fix. No inline comments; review body was empty but the approval was substantive given the reviewer's domain. No post-approval commits were added to the PR.
evidence.security: This is a security vulnerability fix. The previous code treated an empty LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY the same as unset, which caused it to fall back to LEMONADE_API_KEY. However, the authentication check then allowed an empty auth_token to match against admin_api_key_ (which was an empty std::string), effectively bypassing authentication on API and metrics routes. The fix adds a guard: if admin_api_key_ is empty, the condition short-circuits to true (reject). Additionally, the environment variable is now checked for non-empty content (*admin_api_key_env) before being used, preventing the fallback to an empty string. CodeQL analysis passed with no findings. This is the right fix for the vulnerability.
evidence.tests: New regression test test_000_empty_admin_key_does_not_bypass_http_auth() added to test/server_websocket_auth.py. It sets LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY='' and LEMONADE_API_KEY=correct, then exercises /api/v1/health and /internal/routes with three credential scenarios (no header, empty Bearer, wrong Bearer) expecting 401, plus the correct key expecting 200. The existing test suite also covers the admin-only configuration (LEMONADE_API_KEY empty, LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY set). No existing tests were weakened or deleted.

maintainer_todos.text: Start the server with LEMONADE_API_KEY set to a non-empty value and LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY explicitly empty, then send a GET request to /api/v1/health without an Authorization header and confirm it returns HTTP 401.
With the same configuration, send a GET request to /internal/routes with Authorization: Bearer wrong-key and confirm it returns HTTP 401.
With the same configuration, send a GET request to /api/v1/health with Authorization: Bearer matching the LEMONADE_API_KEY value and confirm it returns HTTP 200.

subject: fix(server): prevent auth bypass with an empty admin API key (#4122)
summary: Prevents authentication bypass when LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY is explicitly set to an empty string while LEMONADE_API_KEY is configured, by treating an empty admin key as unset and falling back to the regular API key.
verdict_reason: This is a security fix that changes authentication behavior for a misconfiguration; although the diff and tests are small and correct, no human exercised the empty admin key path on a built server before merge.
